BURSEVI:v4p319#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p319#3/r3.claim: The ruined towns remain beside a stable, traveled route between Mecca and Syria, so Quraysh should take warning when journeying to Syria because their traces have not disappeared.
BURSEVI:v4p319#3/r3.anchor: لبسبيل مقيم أي طريق ثابت يسلكه الناس ويرون آثار تلك البلاد بين مكة والشام

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The expression sabīl muqīm means a commonly trodden way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Quraysh are urged to learn from ruined nations, whose remains they pass on trade routes; Sodom and Gomorrah lay on the Hijaz–Syria route.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: They actually observe their remnants on the trade-routes they often pass by. It may be kept in mind that the settlements of Sodom and Gamorrah were situated on the trade routes of Ḥijāz and Syria.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r23.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r23.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd take the pronoun in وإنها as the destroyed city, which lies on a visible road for those who reflect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r23.anchor: والضمير في وإنها عائد على المدينة المهلكة أي: أنها لبطريق ظاهر بين للمعتبر قاله: مجاهد، وقتادة، وابن زيد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r24.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r24.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r24.claim: Other possibilities are that وإنها refers to the signs or the stones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r24.anchor: قيل: ويحتمل أن يعود على الآيات، ويحتمل أن يعود على الحجارة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r25.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r25.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r25.claim: A further view makes the pronoun refer to the cry, lying in wait for anyone who repeats the people’s deeds; the author links it to the verse saying it is not far from wrongdoers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r25.anchor: وقيل: عائد على الصيحة أي: وإن الصيحة لبمرصد لمن يعمل عملهم لقوله:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r26.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r26.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r26.claim: لبسبيل means a fixed, visible passage that has not disappeared, allowing people to see it and learn from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r26.anchor: وقوله: لبسبيل أي ممر ثابت، وهي بحيث يراها الناس ويعتبرون بها لم تندرس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r27.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r27.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r27.claim: The preserved route warns Quraysh because they pass by the ruins in the morning and at night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r27.anchor: وهو تنبيه لقريش، وإنكم لتمرون عليهم مصبحين وبالليل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r1.claim: The continuation quotes that the cry is not far from wrongdoers, supporting the preceding interpretation that it awaits those who repeat their deeds.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r2.claim: مقيم may mean known, or it may mean lasting and continuous.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r2.anchor: وقيل: مقيم معلوم. وقيل: معتد دائم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the lasting route as an enduring way of destruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هلاك دائم السلوك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r6.claim: The towns of Lot lie beside a clear, established road.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r6.anchor: {وإنها} يعني: قرى قوم لوط {لبسبيل مقيم} أي: بطريق واضح.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r7.claim: Mujahid says the road is marked and cannot be hidden or disappear.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بطريق معلم (2) ليس يخفى ولا زائل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:75-80/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:75-80/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:75-80/r2.claim: The city or villages lie beside a permanent, well-traveled road whose traces people see.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:75-80/r2.anchor: وإن المدينة أو القرى. { لبسبيل مقيم } ثابت يسلكه الناس ويرون آثارها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r6.claim: The overturned cities remain on a clear, fixed road, making reflection easy; Quraysh passed them on some journeys to Syria.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r6.anchor: وإنها } أي هذه المدائن { لبسبيل مقيم * } أي ثابت , وهو مع ذلك مبين

BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r11.claim: An imām here is a clear, enduring path that people follow; it displays God’s greatness and defense of his messengers, and its traces have not vanished.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r11.anchor: بحيث إنه من شدة وضوحه موضح لعظمة الله وانتصاره لأبيائه ممن يكذبهم , وهو مع وضوحه مقيم في مكانه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r12.claim: The passage uses ihtibāk: “fixed” in the first description implies “clear” omitted there, while “clear” in the second implies “fixed” omitted there.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r12.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر في الأولى { مقيم } دلالة على حذف مثله ثانيا , وفي الثانية { مبين } دلالة على حذف مثله أولا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p371/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p371/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p371/r1.claim: The clipped opening preserves a quoted fragment mentioning the earth, two thousand years, and sinners of the Prophet’s community, but its full claim is not recoverable here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p371/r1.anchor: والأرض منذ ألفي سنة لعصاة أمتي

JISHUMI:v6p3973/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r1.speaker: الحسن، وقتادة، والضحاك، ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r1.claim: The signs and the settled route are clear to people who have seen the remains and heard the reports about Lot's people.
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r1.anchor: شاهد فسمع الأخبار، عن الحسن، وقتادة، والضحاك، ومجاهد.

JISHUMI:v6p3973/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r2.speaker: الأصم، وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r2.claim: Alternatively, the signs are known and enduring.
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r2.anchor: وقيل: تلك الآيات معلومة قائمة، عن الأصم، وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v6p3973/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r3.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r3.claim: Qatāda locates the dwellings of Lot's people between Medina and Syria.
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: دور قوم لوط بين المدينة والشام

JISHUMI:v6p3973/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r8.claim: The verses show that Lot's people were destroyed and the believing members of his household were saved.
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r8.anchor: تدل الآية على إهلاك قوم لوط ونجاة من آمن من أهله

JISHUMI:v6p3973/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r10.claim: The remains endure so people can learn from them, and they provide divine لطف for us.
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r10.anchor: وتدل على أن آثارها باقية ليعتبر بها، وأن فيها لطف لنا

MUQATIL:15:74-77/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:15:74-77/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:15:74-77/r4.claim: Lot's ruined towns lie on a clear, enduring route between Mecca and Syria that Meccans and others travel.
MUQATIL:15:74-77/r4.anchor: قرى لوط التى أهلكت بطريق مستقيم، يعني واضح مقيم يمر عليها أهل مكة وغيرهم، وهي بين مكة والشام

RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r7.claim: The pronoun in “it is on an enduring road” returns to Lot's city; its visible, undimmed ruins remain on the route from the Ḥijāz to Syria.
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r7.anchor: الضمير في قوله : { وإنها } عائد إلى مدينة قوم لوط

STUDYQURAN:15:75/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:75/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:15:75/r2.claim: The standing path is a traveled road where people can see the vestiges of Lot’s destroyed people.
STUDYQURAN:15:75/r2.anchor: a road upon which people travel, where they can see the vestiges of the destroyed people of Lot (Aj).

ZAJJAJ:v3p184/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p184/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p184/r5.claim: The remains of the town lie by a clear, evident road.

THALABI:v5p345/r22.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p345/r22.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p345/r22.claim: The destroyed towns of Lot remained beside a clear, permanent road.
THALABI:v5p345/r22.anchor: وإنها يعني قرى قوم لوط لبسبيل مقيم بطريق واضح

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:75-81/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:75-81/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:75-81/r2.claim: Lot's town lies on a lasting, unmistakable road that Quraysh take toward Syria.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:75-81/r2.anchor: يعني: مدينة قوم لوط { لبسبيل مقيم } على طريق قومك إلى الشام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r1.claim: “It” refers to the city of Lot’s people, mentioned earlier in 15:67.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r1.anchor: يعني مدينة قوم لوط، وقد سبق ذكرها في قوله: {وجاء أهل المدينة} [الحجر: 67]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the city lies on your people’s road toward Syria, a familiar route.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: على طريق قومك إلى الشام (¬3)، يريد لبسبيل معروف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r3.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r3.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak take the phrase as a clear road that is neither obliterated nor hidden, remaining open to travelers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة ومجاهد والضحاك: بطريق واضح (¬4)، ومعناه: طريق لا يندرس ولا يخفى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r4.claim: The persistent traces make it possible to take a lesson from the city.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r4.anchor: ومعنى الآية: أن الاعتبار بها ممكن لأن الآثار التي يستدل بها مقيمة ثابتة بها

SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r1.claim: The apparent referent of the pronoun is the city or the towns.
SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r1.anchor: الظاهر عود الضمير على المدينة أو القرى

SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r2.claim: Another proposed referent for the pronoun is the stones.

SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r3.claim: A further proposed referent for the pronoun is the signs.

ASAD-NOTES:15:75#n55/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:75#n55/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:75#n55/r1.claim: Asad identifies the road as running from northern Hijaz to Syria along the Dead Sea; aerial photographs published by the American School of Oriental Research confirmed its trace.
ASAD-NOTES:15:75#n55/r1.anchor: The existence of that road, which led from northern Hijaz to Syria, skirting the Dead Sea

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r1.claim: The pronoun may refer to the destroyed city or the destroyed towns.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r2.claim: The phrase means they lie on a fixed road that people travel and where they can see the ruins.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r2.anchor: أي طريق ثابت يسلكه الناس ويرون آثارها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r3.claim: Other proposed antecedents are the signs, stones, or cry; if the cry, it lies in wait for those who act as they did.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r3.anchor: وقيل : الضمير للآيات وقيل : للحجارة وقيل : للصيحة أي وإن الصيحة لبمرصد لمن يعمل عملهم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r4.claim: Muqīm is glossed as known or lasting, continually traveled along.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r4.anchor: قيل معلوم وقيل : معتد دائم السلوك

DURR-FULL:v5p91/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p91/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p91/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the place’s being on a lasting road as a route to destruction.
DURR-FULL:v5p91/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وإنها لبسبيل مقيم} يقول: لبهلاك

DURR-FULL:v5p91/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p91/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p91/r3.claim: Mujāhid instead explains the phrase as a clear, well-known road.
DURR-FULL:v5p91/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {وإنها لبسبيل مقيم} يقول: لبطريق واضح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r14.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r14.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd take the pronoun to refer to the destroyed city, on a clear, known route.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r14.anchor: والضمير في قوله وإنها يحتمل أن يعود على المدينة المهلكة، أي أنها في طريق ظاهر بين للمعتبر، وهذا تأويل مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r15.claim: The pronoun might instead refer to the signs or the stones; the latter is supported by a report that punishment stones hang between heaven and earth, whose quotation is cut off in the source.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r15.anchor: ويحتمل أن يعود على الآيات، ويحتمل أن يعود على الحجارة، ويقوي هذا التأويل ما روي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r2.claim: The ruined town of Sodom, overturned physically and morally and pelted with stones until it became a foul lake, lies beside a clear, well-traveled route that remains in use.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r2.anchor: وقوله: {وإنها لبسبيل مقيم} أي: وإن قرية سدوم التي أصابها ما أصابها من القلب الصوري والمعنوي،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r3.claim: The established route beside the town is linked to the statement that people pass the destroyed cities morning and night.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r3.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {وإنكم لتمرون عليهم مصبحين وبالليل أفلا تعقلون} [الصافات: 137، 138]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r4.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r4.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak gloss the phrase as meaning that the route is marked or recognizable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد، والضحاك: {وإنها لبسبيل مقيم} قال: معلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r5.claim: Qatada explains the route as clear and open.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: بطريق واضح. وقال قتادة أيضا: بصقع من الأرض واحد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r6.claim: Qatada also says the place is in a single region of the earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة أيضا: بصقع من الأرض واحد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r7.claim: Al-Suddi takes the phrase to mean that Sodom is in a manifest register, as in 36:12, but Ibn Kathir says that is not the intended sense here.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: بكتاب مبين، يعني كقوله: {وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين} [يس: 12] ولكن ليس المعنى على ما قال هاهنا،

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as enduring destruction.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses it as lying on a marked road.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r3.claim: The pronoun refers to the people of Lot’s towns and the people of the Thicket, Shuʿayb’s community.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r3.anchor: بقوله { وإنما } أهل مدائن قوم لوط وأصحاب الأيكة قوم شعيب

MUJAHID:v1p342#5/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p342#5/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p342#5/r1.claim: Mujahid says the site lay beside a clearly marked road.
MUJAHID:v1p342#5/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ وإنها لبسبيل مقيم ﴾ يقول بطريق معلم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p246#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246#3/r1.claim: The pronoun means the towns' visible remains on a fixed route, still seen and not erased.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ وإنها ﴾ وإن هذه القرى يعنى آثارها ﴿ لبسبيل مقيم ﴾ ثابت يسلكه الناس لم يندرس بعدوهم يبصرون تلك الآثار

NASAFI-FULL:v2p246#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246#3/r2.claim: The ruins warn Quraysh, as does the reminder that they pass destroyed towns morning and night.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246#3/r2.anchor: وهو تنبيه لقريش كقوله وانكم لتمرون عليهم مصبحين وبالليل

QURTUBI-FULL:15:76-79/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:76-79/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:76-79/r1.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to the towns of Lot's people.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:76-79/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:76-79/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:76-79/r2.claim: They lie on a lasting road your people take toward Syria.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:76-79/r2.anchor: أي على طريق قومك يا محمد إلى الشام
